current: Backpressure exists as bounded-buffer refusal, not as receiver-granted credit windows. qip_transport::queue::OutboundQueue refuses TransportError::QueueFull at capacity rather than growing (backend/crates/libs/qip-transport/src/queue.rs), and qip_transport::mesh::MeshInbox answers Admission::Full when its bounded capacity is reached (backend/crates/libs/qip-transport/src/mesh.rs:229-240) — the producer discovers backpressure only by being refused at a full buffer, which is precisely the mechanism the requirement's own rationale contrasts with receiver-granted credit ('the only backpressure is a full buffer somewhere').
gap: No credit/window concept exists on any session — a receiver never grants a producer a window of credit up front; the producer only learns it has exceeded capacity when a send is refused.
verification: cargo test -p qip-transport --test reliability a_full_outbound_queue_refuses_by_name_rather_than_growing proves the bounded-refusal mechanism that exists today; a credit-window test does not exist.
notes: verify: status unchanged (PARTIAL). What exists is backpressure, not credit: the mesh publisher is stop-and-wait with one message in flight and backs off on 503 (qip-transport mesh.rs module doc), and MeshInbox serves only on a poll, cut at a server batch limit. PollRequest (mesh.rs:164-172) carries no subscriber-granted window. deployable true -> false: both ends run only in qip-api's mesh backbone (QIP_MESH_CELLS unset in every environment) and in qip-edge-node (execution_nodes = {}).

gap: HMAC authenticates a shared-key producer; it is not a signature a consumer can verify without holding the signing key itself, which is what 'signed by its authorised producer, verified by the consumer' requires. Asymmetric signing is one of the three gaps ADR 0043 names as closable only by a dependency record, not by in-tree code.
